newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lane Crawford to close Singapore shop.
newsitem.headline: Lane Crawford to close Singapore shop.

text.p: Hong Kong retailer Lane Crawford will be giving up its lease at Lane Crawford Place, said David Lawrence, managing director of Marco Polo Developments Ltd on Monday.
Marco Polo, which owns Lane Crawford Place, said in a statement that Lane Crawford would terminate its lease on the premises on October 1.
Both Marco Polo and Lane Crawford are controlled by Hong Kong's New Asia Realty and Trust Company Ltd.
Lane Crawford's closure comes almost a year after the company decided to reduce by half the floor space in the loss-making department store.
Marco Polo said Lane Crawford had informed it that "further losses have been suffered and its trading has not improved since the downsizing exercise last year".
Lane Crawford had wanted a further reduction in the area it leased "to reduce its overheads and to operate as an exclusive specialty store concept", it said.

Marco Polo said it had not agreed, saying it could increase its rental revenue by leasing space to more, smaller stores, and would continue to "run the risk of Lane Crawford defaulting on rental and service charges".

Lane Crawford had agreed to pay a lump sum payment of Singapore $3.15 million in compensation for the expected loss of rents Marco Polo would incur during the time taken to convert the two storeys occupied by Lane Crawford into smaller shops.
Marco Polo said the estimated cost of conversion would be about S$6.3 million.
